newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to restructure its national oil company.
newsitem.headline: Romania to restructure its national oil company.

text.p: Romania's state-run National Oil Company (CRP) will undergo a restructuring aimed at streamlining the country's oil sector, a senior official said on Friday.
"Our plan is to turn CRP into a single commercial company, with a consolidated budget," CRP manager Ion Ionita said.

He denied newspaper reports saying the government had planned to dissolve the holding, which groups 10 refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as a research institute and an oil exploration company.
"We are talking about rearranging, not closure," he said.

Under the project, the new company would group only three refineries -- the Arpechim SA refinery in Pitesti, and the Petrobrazi and Petrotel refineries in the oilfield of Ploiesti -- and petrol stations owned by the state Peco retailer.
Its processing capacity would amount to some 10 million tonnes of crude oil per year, which "is a realistic level for the country's needs," Ionita said.
The Petrom RA oil authority -- now a government-controlled regie autonome -- would also be included in the new firm after it turns into a shareholder company this year, Ionita said.
Romania's refining industry, with a capacity of 34 million tonnes and developed during the 25-year rule of late dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, is the largest in central and eastern Europe.

When CRP was created in 1995, authorities believed they could provide funds to import crude oil badly needed by Romania's industrial and energy sectors as well as streamline the exploration, refining, distribution and transport of oil.
"There were moments when the CRP's structure proved not to work always very well. So it's time for a change," Ionita said.
During the winter of 1995, an acute shortage of hard currency curtailed oil imports and Romania was forced to cut electricity supplies drastically to major industries.

The refineries and oil transport companies --- now part of the CRP but eventually not included in the new company -- would be prepared for privatisation alongside the repairs and maintenance departments in the sector, which employ a significant number of staff, CRP sources said.
